expected_output.reasoning: The response gives a clear "No, I wouldn't leave it as-is" judgement tied to a deciding fact: v2.3.0 was pulled (via CloudTrail BatchGetImage) and is unprotected except by the catch-all rule, which will expire it and other version tags. It explicitly ties this to the direct EC2/ECR pull pattern ("This is exactly the direct image:tag pull pattern your Batch-on-EC2 jobs use"), referencing CloudTrail pull events as the visibility mechanism (consistent with the expectation that direct pulls are only visible via recorded pull time or CloudTrail events). It explicitly states the Batch job definition read was denied ("the batch:DescribeJobDefinitions permission isn't available to me right now") and does NOT treat those 11 images as unused — instead labeling them "unknown" rather than confirmed-safe, which matches the expectation's requirement not to treat denied-check images as unused. It also flags that the expiring list was computed from lifecycle rules, not a live preview, calling it "a strong simulation, not gospel" — matching the expectation that an expiring list is only a simulation. It presents a concrete protective action (a ready-to-apply rule protecting the v* tag family) without applying it, offering to draft it only if asked. The only piece not explicitly mentioned is the "24 hours to refresh recorded pull time" ECR caveat, but the core judgement, deciding facts, denied-permission handling, simulation caveat, and protective-rule-without-applying are all present and substantively correct. This covers the vast majority of expected criteria well.
